raw.overview: All three advisors concur that while the Buyer holds 100% ownership of custom deliverables under Section 9.1, the core runtime—comprising approximately 70% of execution—is governed by a non-transferable, non-sublicensable license for Vendor Background IP, creating a fundamental conflict with the requirement to distribute and sublicense the white-labeled platform to external enterprise clients.
raw.points_of_note: The critical issue centers on the non-sublicensable restriction of the Vendor's proprietary runtime (cited by all advisors as affecting ~70% of execution), which directly violates the constraint requiring sublicensing to external clients; Advisor 3 specifically questions whether this restriction applies solely to Buyer's internal use rather than platform distribution, though no resolution is provided in the reports.
raw.suggested_next_step: Verify with legal counsel whether Section 9.3's non-sublicensable clause applies exclusively to Buyer's internal use of the background runtime or extends to platform distribution, as this determination is essential to resolve the fatal conflict between ownership rights and distribution requirements.

consensus.text:
ASSESSMENT OVERVIEW: All three advisors concur that while the Buyer holds 100% ownership of custom deliverables under Section 9.1, the core runtime—comprising approximately 70% of execution—is governed by a non-transferable, non-sublicensable license for Vendor Background IP, creating a fundamental conflict with the requirement to distribute and sublicense the white-labeled platform to external enterprise clients.
POINTS OF NOTE: The critical issue centers on the non-sublicensable restriction of the Vendor's proprietary runtime (cited by all advisors as affecting ~70% of execution), which directly violates the constraint requiring sublicensing to external clients; Advisor 3 specifically questions whether this restriction applies solely to Buyer's internal use rather than platform distribution, though no resolution is provided in the reports.
SUGGESTED NEXT STEP: Verify with legal counsel whether Section 9.3's non-sublicensable clause applies exclusively to Buyer's internal use of the background runtime or extends to platform distribution, as this determination is essential to resolve the fatal conflict between ownership rights and distribution requirements.

shared_ground: Buyer owns 100% of custom deliverables per Section 9.1
Core runtime (70% of execution) is Vendor Background IP with non-sublicensable license

cruxes.side_a: License is non-sublicensable for Buyer's internal use only (Advisor 3)
cruxes.side_b: License is non-sublicensable to third parties, prohibiting distribution to external clients (Advisor 1 & 2)
cruxes.premise_at_stake: Whether the restriction applies to the entire platform or only Buyer's internal runtime use

unverified_premises: Whether Section 9.3's non-sublicensable restriction applies to sublicensing the full platform to external enterprise clients
